transcription.covers: Head II Articles I-IX and Rejection of Errors I-VII, English, with page anchors
transcription.method: manual transfer from OCR output; OCR artifacts preserved verbatim
collatedAgainst: articlesofsynodo1841syno_djvu.xml chunks 43-45: second OCR rendering of the same scan, printed pages 280-297; zero divergence from the transfer except three recorded corrections (perseveringiy->perseveringly, garbled 'Man' in art. IV, letter 'S.' as the article-8 numeral)
Schaff/CCEL creeds3.txt chunk 165: Latin original of Head II artt. I-IX + Rejectio I-VII; each preserved OCR artifact resolved against the Latin
English translation of 1840 (Reformed Protestant Dutch Church): independent second English witness for Articles I-IX, now in Git as ИСКУПЛЕНИЕ/16_DORT_HEAD_II_ENGLISH_1840_PRIMARY_TEXT.md
collationFindings: Rejectio IV as printed by Scott is ABRIDGED: the Latin closing clause 'Et cum impio Socino, novam et peregrinam hominis coram Deo justificationem, contra totius Ecclesiae consensum, inducunt' is absent; full text only in Latin
Rejectio III: the Schaff/CCEL Latin reads 'nullis certo meruisse', an artifact of that edition; Scott's English and the sense require 'non certo meruisse' - here the English controls the Latin
Rejectio I: Latin 'in Dei Patris sapientiam' vs Scott 'the wisdom of God' - translational difference, not doctrinal
Article III: Latin 'unica'; the 1840 translation has 'the only and most perfect sacrifice', Scott has 'a single and most perfect sacrifice' - quote 'only', not 'single'
Article VIII, the key line for 13 §1.2: Latin, Scott 1841 and the 1840 translation agree that the efficacy is 'in all the elect ... to them alone'
